scope.summary: Implement full-body IK posing with pins per Section 13.18 (BK-18.3, TAI-BK-063), closing the Daz Active-Pose parity gap and AREQ-017: hands, feet, and knees pinnable while dragging any other part, reusing the existing FABRIK/2-bone solver lane (13.7 avatar pose editing) but driving the BodyKit SKELETON itself, not merely collision capsules; IK reach percentages and pin translation/rotation locks are parameters, not code switches.
acceptance_criteria: solve_ik(skeleton_pose, effector_targets, pins, params) drives the canonical BodyKit skeleton bone chain transforms; the FABRIK/2-bone implementations are reused from the existing avatar lane (no duplicate solver, import-path assertion).

IkPin {bone_name, lock_translation, lock_rotation, reach_pct} holds a pinned bone within tolerance while other effectors drag: pinned hands/feet/knees move less than the documented tolerance during a pelvis drag test.
Solve honors per-chain joint limits from the skeleton def (no hyperextension past declared limits in the fixture poses).
IK solving works headlessly through a typed API (pose-in/pose-out, no GUI dependency) and is deterministic for identical inputs.
IK results are ordinary BodyPoseAsset-compatible bone transforms consumable by MT-520 pose authority.
scope.risk_if_missed: Weak IK is a top community complaint about Daz posing; without pinned full-body IK on the real skeleton, posing multi-contact adult scenes (hands planted, hips driving) becomes per-bone FK drudgery and the MT-521 multi-actor lane has no solver to stand on.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
